scope_label: justification for a specified test-score interpretation and use
definition: A validity argument is a reasoned case that evidence and assumptions support a specified interpretation or use of test results for a stated population and purpose.
explanation: It connects each important inference to relevant evidence and explains why the proposed action follows. Possible counterevidence and limits matter because the same scores can be used for different purposes.
A folder of studies is not a validity argument unless the studies bear on the claims being made. New uses or populations can require a revised argument.
